subject: Proposal: layered-tenor ramp smoothing & optional auto-extension for Atlas.ai
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@atlas.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: layered-tenor ramp smoothing & optional auto-extension for Atlas.ai

Hi Alec —

Following up on our renewal window for the Oct 31 term. We took your usage telemetry and last quarter’s burst patterns into account and put together a flexible structure that aims to give Atlas predictability while preserving runway for your platform team. Attached is a short proposal (redwood-layered-term-proposal.pdf) and a 2-sheet usage schedule for your review. High-level summary below: 

- Term options: 24-month preferred (option to opt into 18-month at same commercial band)
- Commit structure: layered annual commits with quarterly true-ups (Q1 conservative, Q2/Q3 ramp to expected production load)
- Ramp smoothing: we’ll apply quarterly true-up windows + one-time frontloaded migration credits to cover onboarding bursts
- Auto-extension: optional 90-day auto-extension that can be toggled at renewal; requires legal sign-off for opt-in
- Co-terming: we can anchor a master contract and attach subaccount annexes so other Atlas business units can co-term without duplicative SLAs
- Burst buffer & SLO credits: 3-month burst buffer and up to 5% SLO credit in first quarter if we miss latency SLOs during migration

Numbers in the attached PDF include: Year 1 commit = 150M tokens, Year 2 = 200M tokens with graduated discounting and an overage rate schedule. We also included a scenario showing an 18-month alternate that frontloads a higher commit in month 1-6 to cover migration spikes.

Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through the proposal and confirm whether you want the 18m option surfaced to Legal? I’m available Wed 9/7 10:00–12:00 or Fri 9/9 13:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-layered-term-proposal.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
Attachment: atlas-usage-schedule.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)

From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@atlas.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, contracts@atlas.ai
Date: 2027-09-03T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: layered-tenor ramp smoothing & optional auto-extension for Atlas.ai

Kimberly —

Appreciate the thorough breakdown and the model scenarios. A few quick points from our side: 

1) Term preference: our platform team is lukewarm on a hard 24-month lock. We’d prefer an 18-month with an option to extend to 24 (if performance and unit economics hold). Is pricing parity possible between the two?

2) Co-terming: good idea to have a master with annexes — that would simplify procurement. We’ll need to confirm whether the other BU wants to be bound by the same SLOs.

3) Auto-extension: Legal flagged auto-extension language as a risk unless there’s a clear opt-in. Please send the proposed clause and an explicit opt-out flow. Our contracts team is contracts@atlas.ai — I’ve cc’d them.

4) Credits & costs: can you itemize the migration/top-up credits and give a ballpark cost per 1M tokens under both year-1 and year-2 pricing? That will help procurement do a quick comparator.

We can do a call Thurs 9/9 11:00 PT if that works for your team.

—Alec
Alec Turner
Head of AI Platform, Atlas.ai
alec.turner@atlas.ai | +1 212-555-0199

On Thu, Sep 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message and attachments]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas renewal — suggested counter and ask list

Team — forwarding Alec’s notes. Quick internal proposed approach before the 9/9 call: 

- Commercial: present two priced options side-by-side (18m and 24m) but keep unit economics aligned so we don’t create a heavy price arbitrage. Recommend list pricing: Year1 effective $0.95 / 1k tokens (baseline) with graduated discounts applied in year 2 for the 24m option.
- Migration credits: offer a one-time credit equivalent to 40M tokens (to be applied against first true-up) and a $15k onboarding professional services credit to cover initial burst tuning — this addresses their migration spike ask.
- Burst buffer: allow a 20% month-1 buffer applied as non-billable for first 90 days; additional overage billed at pre-agreed overage rate.
- Co-terming: structure as Master Services Agreement (MSA) + Annex A per subaccount. Annex can include opt-out for distinct SLOs.
- Auto-extension: draft opt-in language that requires express customer acceptance or a DocuSign toggle; request Legal to accept opt-in only.
- Implementation: include a 30-day planning window and quarterly true-up cadence (30 days post-quarter close).

Attachments: redlines_initial.docx (proposed legal language for auto-extension and true-up windows), atlas-usage-schedule.xlsx (worked example with quarterly ramp).

Replies inline: 

Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>: OK — I’d push a 12% first-year discount for the 24m if they commit to the master + annex approach.

Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>: +1 on the buffer; also propose we include an option to switch part of the commit onto Dedicated capacity after month 6 if usage exceeds threshold. That reduces their unit cost and signals technical commitment.

Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>: Add a clause that allows limited cross-subaccount bursting for the first 6 months to reduce friction.

Action: I’ll surface this during the 9/9 call and send a revised PDF immediately after.

-Kim

Attachment: redlines_initial.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Revised proposal & next steps (DocuSign link) — Atlas.ai renewal

Alec / Atlas Legal —

Thanks again for the call on 9/9. Per our discussion, attached is the revised proposal and a short summary of the two term paths (18m vs 24m) plus the specific opt-in auto-extension language we propose for Legal to review. Key changes from the original: 

- Pricing: we aligned unit economics so the 18m and 24m options are adjacent — no large parity gap.
- Credits: one-time migration credit = 40M token equivalent (applied to first true-up). PS credit = $15k.
- Ramp / true-ups: quarterly true-up cadence with 30-day reconciliation window; 90-day non-billable buffer for month 1–3.
- Co-terming: MSA + Annex approach included; Annex template attached for your procurement to review.
- Auto-extension: opt-in clause is explicit and requires customer signature at DocuSign link below. No silent renewals.

DocuSign (proposal + opt-in toggle): https://www.docusign.com/sign?doc=DW-4227-ATLAS
Drive (proposal + annex + schedule): https://drive.redwood.com/s/renewals/atlas-proposal

Please confirm preferred term (18m or 24m) and whether Procurement wants a single master with annex or separate contracts per BU. If Legal has redlines on the auto-extension clause, please send them back to me at contracts@redwood.com and I’ll loop in Redwood Legal.

If we get confirmation by EOD Fri 9/17 we can lock pricing and get a signature timeline that hits an Oct 15 execution target (to avoid any gap ahead of 10/31).

Best —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
